SOURCE: BitNet b1.58 2B4T Technical Report. Shuming Ma*, Hongyu Wang*, Shaohan Huang, Xingxing Zhang, Ying Hu, Ting Song, Yan Xia, Furu Wei (Microsoft Research / Tsinghua). arXiv:2504.12285v2, 25 Apr 2025. Preprint.
COVERAGE: All 14 pages read (45,584 chars): body, conclusion, future work, references (skimmed for origins), Appendix A (baseline links) and B (eval pipeline, energy and latency setup). Nothing skipped. Figure 1 is a chart with no extractable numbers; I did not run the figure-caption script, and the caption is quoted below. Extraction was clean. No embedded instructions found.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Native ternary 2B model, 4T tokens, is roughly on par with full-precision peers on average score.
 number: Avg 54.19 vs Qwen2.5-1.5B 55.23, SmolLM2-1.7B 48.70, LLaMA-3.2-1B 44.90, Gemma-3-1B 43.74, MiniCPM-2B 42.05
 setup: Table 1; 16 benchmarks; all instruction-tuned checkpoints; authors re-ran everything with public pipelines. Metrics differ by task (0-shot, 5-shot, etc.).
 quote: "Average 44.90 43.74 55.23 48.70 42.05 54.19" (column order LLaMA 3.2 1B, Gemma-3 1B, Qwen2.5 1.5B, SmolLM2 1.7B, MiniCPM 2B, BitNet 2B)
 where: p.6, Table 1
2. Non-embedding memory is 0.4GB, versus 1.4 to 4.8GB for the full-precision peers.
 number: 0.4GB vs 2GB / 1.4GB / 2.6GB / 3.2GB / 4.8GB
 setup: non-embedding weights only, so embeddings are excluded. Order is LLaMA 1B, Gemma-3 1B, Qwen2.5 1.5B, SmolLM2 1.7B, MiniCPM 2B.
 quote: "Memory 2GB 1.4GB 2.6GB 3.2GB 4.8GB 0.4GB (Non-emb)"
 where: p.6, Table 1
3. CPU decoding latency is 29ms per token, versus 41 to 124ms.
 number: 29ms TPOT vs 48 / 41 / 65 / 67 / 124ms
 setup: Surface Laptop Studio 2, Intel Core i7-13800H, 8 threads. BitNet ran on bitnet.cpp and the others on llama.cpp. 128 tokens generated, average latency per token. This compares different inference stacks, and the precision of the llama.cpp baselines is not stated.
 quote: "Latency 48ms 41ms 65ms 67ms 124ms 29ms (CPU; TPOT)"; "the BitNet b1.58 2B4T model was tested using its bitnet.cpp implementation, whereas other models were evaluated using the llama.cpp framework. For each model, we generated 128 tokens and report the average latency per token for this task."
 where: p.6 Table 1; p.14 Appendix B
4. Estimated energy is 0.028J, versus 0.186 to 0.649J (about 9x lower than the nearest, Gemma-3 1B).
 number: 0.028J vs 0.258 / 0.186 / 0.347 / 0.425 / 0.649J
 setup: analytical estimate, not measured. It counts arithmetic operations only (the paper calls this AOE), using the Horowitz 2014 / Zhang 2022 energy model at 7nm, with sequence length 512. It ignores memory-access energy.
 quote: "Energy 0.258J 0.186J 0.347J 0.425J 0.649J 0.028J (Estimated)"; Table 4: "FP16 0.16 0.34 / INT8 0.007 0.07" (ADD pJ, MUL pJ); "The sequence length is set as 512 tokens."
 where: p.6 and p.14
5. Against post-training INT4 quantization of Qwen2.5-1.5B, BitNet is smaller. Its accuracy is higher than INT4 and slightly below bf16 on the 3-task average.
 number: memory 0.4GB vs 0.7GB (GPTQ-int4 and AWQ-int4) vs 2.6GB (bf16). Avg 55.01 vs 55.72 bf16 / 52.15 GPTQ / 51.17 AWQ. MMLU 53.17 vs 60.25 / 58.06 / 57.43. GSM8K 58.38 vs 56.79 / 50.57 / 50.64. IFEval 53.48 vs 50.12 / 47.84 / 45.44.
 setup: Table 2; only 3 benchmarks (MMLU 5-shot, GSM8K 4-shot, IFEval 0-shot). The Qwen variants keep bf16 activations; BitNet uses int8.
 quote: "Memory 2.6GB 0.7GB 0.7GB 0.4GB (Non-emb)"; "Average 55.72 52.15 51.17 55.01"; "Standard PTQ techniques lead to a noticeable degradation in performance compared to the original full-precision model."
 where: p.7, Table 2
 note: BitNet's 55.01 is below Qwen bf16's 55.72. The text says it "maintains stronger overall performance than the INT4 quantized versions".
6. Among open 1-bit models, BitNet 2B4T is clearly best, including against much larger models post-training-quantized to 1.58 bit.
 number: Avg over 11 benchmarks: BitNet 60.68, Falcon3-1.58bit-7B 50.76, Llama3-8B-1.58 49.75, Bonsai-0.5B 41.06, OLMo-Bitnet-1B 32.22
 setup: Table 3. Bonsai and OLMo-Bitnet are native 1-bit but smaller. Falcon3 and Llama3-8B are PTQ'd to 1.58 bit, not native.
 quote: "Average 41.06 32.22 50.76 49.75 60.68"
 where: p.7, Table 3
7. Per-benchmark picture in Table 1 (BitNet 2B vs others): BitNet leads on ARC-Challenge 49.91, PIQA 77.09, WinoGrande 71.90 and GSM8K 58.38. It trails Qwen2.5-1.5B on MMLU (53.17 vs 60.25), HumanEval+ (38.40 vs 50.60), MATH-500 (43.40 vs 53.00) and CommonsenseQA (71.58 vs 76.41). It trails on IFEval (53.48 vs 66.67 Gemma-3), TriviaQA (33.57 vs 45.97 SmolLM2) and MT-bench (5.85 vs 6.57 MiniCPM).
 setup: Table 1.
 quote: "ARC-Challange 37.80 38.40 46.67 43.52 44.80 49.91"; "GSM8K 38.21 31.16 56.79 45.11 4.40 58.38"; "MMLU 45.58 39.91 60.25 49.24 51.82 53.17"; "HumanEval+ 31.10 37.20 50.60 28.00 43.90 38.40"
 where: p.6
8. Training-token comparison. BitNet used 4T tokens. LLaMA 3.2 1B used 9T, Gemma-3 1B 2T, Qwen2.5 1.5B 18T, SmolLM2 1.7B 11T, MiniCPM 1.1T.
 quote: "Training Tokens 9T 2T 18T 11T 1.1T 4T (Pre-training)" with the annotations "(pruning & distillation)" and "(distillation)" (the extraction leaves it unclear which model each annotation belongs to).
 where: p.6

METHOD DETAILS (for notes)
- BitLinear replaces nn.Linear. Weights are ternary {-1,0,+1} (1.58 bit) via absmean quantization in the forward pass. Activations are int8 via per-token absmax. subln normalization. Squared ReLU (ReLU2) in the FFN instead of SwiGLU. RoPE. No bias terms. LLaMA 3 tokenizer, 128,256 vocab. The model is trained from scratch, not converted.
- Pre-training has two stages. Stage 1 uses a high peak LR with cosine decay. Stage 2 is a cooldown "approximately midway through the planned training token count" with an abrupt LR drop and a lower-peak cosine, on higher-quality data. Weight decay is cosine to a peak of 0.1 in stage 1 and zero in stage 2. Data: DCLM, FineWeb-EDU, synthetic math.
- SFT: WildChat, LMSYS-Chat-1M, WizardLM Evol-Instruct, SlimOrca, plus GLAN and MathScale synthetic data. Loss is summed rather than mean-reduced. It uses a larger LR and more epochs than full-precision models of similar size.
- DPO: UltraFeedback and MagPie data. 2 epochs, LR 2e-7, beta 0.1, Liger Kernel. No PPO/GRPO RL.
- Master weights are bf16 (training only). Packed 1.58-bit weights are for inference. A GGUF is released for bitnet.cpp.
- GPU kernel: four ternary values packed into one int8 in HBM. The kernel loads them to shared memory, unpacks, then multiplies with int8 activations. This is the pack-store-load-unpack-compute scheme, based on the Ladder framework (Wang et al. 2023b). CPU: bitnet.cpp, described as "lossless inference relative to the training procedure". No GPU latency or throughput numbers are given.
- Eval tooling: lm-evaluation-harness for most tasks, evalplus for HumanEval+, a customized math-evaluation-harness for MATH-500, official LLM Judge for MT-Bench. Chat format is used for generative tasks (GSM8K, IFEval, MT-Bench).

LIMITS
- The authors concede current GPUs are not designed for this: "current commodity GPU architectures are not optimally designed for the 1-bit models". Real gains need custom kernels or hardware (see the GPU kernel and bitnet.cpp notes above).
- Scaling behavior is unknown. They list scaling laws and larger models (7B, 13B) as future work and ask "if the performance parity with full-precision models holds".
- Maximum sequence length is limited, which hurts long chain-of-thought. The model is English-centric, with no multilingual or multimodal support. Theory of why it works is open.
- No RL stage, so math and reasoning could improve.
- Memory counts non-embedding parameters only. Energy is an arithmetic-only estimate and not measured. Latency compares bitnet.cpp against llama.cpp on one laptop CPU.
- Not shown: GPU latency and throughput, KV-cache/activation memory, long-context behavior, safety evaluation, and any training cost or training-memory comparison (master weights are bf16).
- The paper claims "on par", but BitNet trails the best peer on average (54.19 vs 55.23) and on MMLU, HumanEval+, MATH-500 and IFEval.
- Table 2 uses only 3 benchmarks. Table 3 uses 11, so the BitNet average there (60.68) is not comparable with Table 1's 54.19.
- The Fig.1 caption says the model "advances the Pareto frontier ... under 3B parameters in terms of performance versus memory", on the average score of 11 benchmarks. Data points are shown only graphically. Models in the figure: LLaMa-3.2-1B, Gemma-3-1B, Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B, SmolLM2-1.7B, MiniCPM-2B.

BUILDS ON
- BitNet (Wang et al., 2023a, "BitNet: Scaling 1-bit transformers"). Ma et al., 2024 (BitNet b1.58; the full reference is not in the text I read).
- Foundation Transformers / subln (Wang et al., 2022).
- Squared ReLU and sparsity: BitNet a4.8 (Wang et al., 2024b) and Q-sparse (Wang et al., 2024a).
- Transformer (Vaswani 2017). RoPE (Su et al., 2024). LLaMA 3 recipe (Dubey et al., 2024). DPO (Rafailov et al., 2023).
- Energy model: Horowitz 2014 and Zhang et al. 2022. Kernels: Ladder (Wang et al. 2023b). CPU: bitnet.cpp (Wang et al., 2025).
- Compared against: OLMo-Bitnet-1B; Falcon3 1.58bit (Team 2024); Bonsai; Llama3-8B-1.58.

CODE: none beyond the chat template. Quoted: "<|begin_of_text|>System: {system_message}<|eot_id|> User: {user_message_1}<|eot_id|> Assistant: {assistant_message_1}<|eot_id|> ..." (p.4). Release: HF bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T (packed), -bf16 (master), -gguf; code at https://aka.ms/bitnet.

FIGURES: Fig. 1 (p.1), scatter of memory footprint (GB, x-axis 0 to 6) against the 11-benchmark average (y-axis 50 to 66), showing BitNet on the Pareto frontier. It is the quick visual for the memory/quality trade-off, but its values are not extractable. Table 4 (p.14) is the ADD/MUL pJ energy table used to derive the energy estimates.

PROBLEMS: None serious. The Table 1 text layout loses which model carries the "(pruning & distillation)" and "(distillation)" annotations. Table 1 spells the benchmark "ARC-Challange" (verbatim from the source). The extraction tool printed in 40,000-char truncated chunks, but the whole text was read through the saved file.
